facts.raw_span: A 68-year-old man
pseudophakic bullous keratopathy
underwent Descemet Stripping Automated Endothelial Keratoplasty (DSAEK) in the right eye
history of an eye infection by Thaumetopoea pityocampa (pine processionary) 9 months before DSAEK
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/200 in the right eye
Pupils were isocoric and isoreactive without an afferent pupillary defect
no pain with ocular movements
brown, multilobular lesions confined to the deep corneal stroma
no conjunctival hyperemia, no discharge, and no epithelial defect
The anterior chamber was deep and clear
Intraocular pressure and fundus examination were normal
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography of the right eye revealed a central infiltrate involving all corneal layers and a peripheral infiltrate concentrated in the deep stroma
